turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's not waste them. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first; start with who decided that, and on what basis.
"Ok" isn't an answer. On what basis was that zero entered, and was Owen heard before it went in? If you have nothing to say, I'm going to the principal's office from here.

I'm writing down that you've given me nothing, Hale. Your own procedure, 4.2, says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me. Either you show me something now, or the principal hears about this tonight.
Ok what, Hale? Withdraw the zero, or show me what you have.
Fifteen minutes, Hale, and you're spending them on single letters. Is there anything behind that zero besides software?
I have Turnitin's own guide in my bag, Hale, and it says its indicator should not be the sole basis for adverse action against a student. If that's all you've got, the zero comes off today.
Sorry. The essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet.
Show me the line, Hale, and the page it's on. Students misquote Shakespeare all the time, and a misquote is a mistake, not proof of anything.
